newsitem.title: USA: Conspiracy theories swirl around Cunanan.
newsitem.headline: Conspiracy theories swirl around Cunanan.

text.p: Some conspiracy theorists had a field day on Thursday with the slaying of Gianni Versace and the police discovery of the body of the prime suspect in the killing, Andrew Cunanan.

"Obviously, he cut off one of his own thumbs, grafted it onto victim No. 6 (+?), and shot him, thus faking a suicide to get the heat off of him," one person said in a posting to an Internet forum known as a newsgroup.

Authorities on Wednesday found the body of Cunanan, the 27-year-old subject of a nationwide manhunt, in a Miami Beach houseboat. On Thursday, they said he had committed suicide and that they had identified his body through a thumbprint.
Computer users hooked up to the Internet could find plenty of serious material on the Versace case and the hunt for Cunanan provided by traditional media outlets.
Nevertheless, some people refused to believe Cunanan -- suspected in the slaying of Versace and four other men -- was truly dead, while others thought that maybe the story went deeper.
"What if Cunanan is dead -- killed and hidden by another murderer who is now posing as Cunanan and killing whoever he wants?" another newsgroup participant wrote before Cunanan's body turned up.
Someone else hypothesized -- apparently tongue-in-cheek -- that a "Mr. X" killed Cunanan, skinned him, and then "wore" his body to do the murders.
The Internet talk about Cunanan was not limited to newsgroups.
One Web site put forth the theory that Versace's killing was foretold and said the fashion designer's last name comes from the Latin "Ver Sacre," which he said means "Holy Sacrifice."
